opportunities.title: CUSG SOAC: Operational funding
opportunities.amount: Part of per-year SOAC cap (about $1,000 new / $5,000 established RSOs); cap figures come from search, not confirmed on the page
opportunities.reasons: The club is a registered CU Boulder RSO open to all students, and SOAC operational funding covers regular operating costs, which fits food and hardware. The fall priority deadline (Oct 14) has passed, but you can still submit on BuffConnect, and the last fall hearing is Nov 18, so meet your CSI liaison and submit now. If you miss it, the next priority deadline is Feb 24 (2027). Funds must be spent by May 1, and the page doesn't confirm the dollar caps or whether "AI tools to give to students" counts as organizational use.
eligibility_flags: Must be open to all CU Boulder students
Priority deadline Oct 14 passed; late submissions possible
Must meet with CSI liaison first

opportunities.title: CUSG SOAC: Event funding
opportunities.amount: Part of per-year SOAC cap (about $1,000 new / $5,000 established RSOs)
opportunities.reasons: The club is a registered student organization open to all students, so it qualifies. SOAC funds events, operations (which can include food) and travel. The Oct 14 priority deadline has passed, but late requests are still accepted with no guaranteed hearing slot, and the last fall hearing is Nov 18. Submit on BuffConnect soon and meet your CSI liaison first. I couldn't confirm the dollar caps on the page, and AI tools or hardware may fit only under operations.
eligibility_flags: Must be open to all students

opportunities.title: Arts & Sciences Student Government (ASSG) funding
opportunities.reasons: The club is a registered CU Boulder RSO, and ASSG gives up to $1,000 per semester through a funding hearing. The club's food, AI tools and hardware needs look like a fit, but I couldn't confirm whether ASSG covers those items. ASSG also only funds clubs affiliated with the Arts & Sciences College, and we don't know if the club is. Email csifinance@colorado.edu or the Center for Student Involvement to check, and the funding request form in BuffConnect has no stated deadline, so submit early.
eligibility_flags: Must follow ASSG bylaws and Student Fee Regulations

opportunities.title: ALL Applied AI Network chapter program
opportunities.reasons: This is not a grant. It's a free chapter program with a dashboard, a sponsor portal, and a way to run reimbursements and payments. You can claim your existing club's chapter and keep your name. The network is run by a 501(c)(3), so the club doesn't need to be one. The club could use it to find sponsors for food, AI tools and hardware, but no dollar amounts are promised and I couldn't confirm how sponsor funding works.
eligibility_flags: Free to join; run by a 501(c)(3) (club need not be one)

opportunities.title: CUSG SOAC: Travel funding
opportunities.reasons: The club is an RSO open to all students, so it can apply. But this fund covers only overnight trips over 60 miles (lodging, transport, registration fees), not food, AI tools or hardware, and the club has no trip planned. The next deadline is Jan 4, 2027 for March travel; apply only if officers plan a conference or competition trip. For food and hardware, SOAC's separate operations funding may fit better.
eligibility_flags: Must be open to all students
Travelers must be full fee-paying students

opportunities.title: iMasons AI Incubator
opportunities.reasons: This isn't a grant. It's a pilot marketplace where company sponsors pay (a rate sheet shows $5,000 to $150,000 a year) so students get cloud capacity, AI tools and GPU hours while working on company projects. The page gives no application process, deadline or cash award, and the only school it names is NYU. It could give members free AI tools and compute, so it's worth a quick email to iMasons, but it won't pay for food or hardware.

opportunities.title: NSF FINDERS FOUNDRY
opportunities.reasons: Only nonprofits, governments, universities (on behalf of faculty) and tribal nations can submit, so a student club can't apply. It also funds K-12 learning and workforce projects led by teams of educators, technologists and researchers, not club food, AI tools or hardware. Not worth pursuing.

opportunities.title: IUSE / Professional Formation of Engineers: RED
opportunities.reasons: This NSF grant funds engineering department overhauls, and the lead applicant must be a Department Chair/Head (or a Dean or Provost). A student club can't apply, and it doesn't pay for food, AI tools or hardware. Skip it.

# AI Club: SOAC Operational Funding Request

## Organization Overview
AI Club is a registered student organization (RSO) at CU Boulder, founded about two years ago and open to all students. It has about 100 members. About 100 people attend meetings, and the email list has 800+ subscribers. The club brings in speakers to teach CU students and faculty about evolving technology, especially AI. It has had engagements with G2 and Techstars.

## Purpose of Request
We are asking SOAC for operational funding for the regular operations that let us carry out our mission:
1. **Food at regular member meetings.** [[MISSING: number of meetings planned and cost per meeting]]
2. **Hardware for research time.** [[ASSUMED: The hardware will be used for organizational purposes and stored on campus.]] [[MISSING: specific hardware items, quantities and vendor quotes]]
3. **AI tools for students.** [[ASSUMED: These are organizational resources, such as shared licenses, that members use through the club.]] [[MISSING: which tools, cost, and how access is distributed]]

## Amount Requested
[[MISSING: total amount requested. The target amount is unknown. Check the SOAC cap for an RSO of our age with your CSI liaison.]]

## Budget
| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Food | [[MISSING: cost]] |
| Hardware | [[MISSING: cost]] |
| AI tools | [[MISSING: cost]] |

## Impact
Operational funds would let the club keep hosting regular meetings for the roughly 100 students who attend. They would also give members the tools and hardware to work on AI. [[MISSING: expected number of students who benefit from the tools and hardware]]

## Timeline
Operational funds must be spent by May 1, 2027. After approval, we will hold a pre-spending meeting with CSI Finance. [[MISSING: spending schedule]]

## Requirements checklist
- [ ] RSO must be open to all CU Boulder students
- [ ] Meet your assigned CSI liaison before submitting
- [ ] Submit the request on BuffConnect
- [ ] Fall priority deadline Oct 14 has passed. You can still submit, but SOAC cannot guarantee a hearing slot. The last fall hearing is Wed Nov 18, 2026
- [ ] Next priority deadline is Wed Feb 24, 2027, for hearings through Mar 31 (the last hearing of the year). Dates are subject to change
- [ ] Attend a SOAC funding hearing; review the SOAC Code and the hearing prep guide
- [ ] Operational funds must be used for organizational (not personal) purposes and stored on campus where possible
- [ ] Hold a pre-spending meeting with CSI Finance after approval
- [ ] Spend all operational funds by Sat May 1, 2027; food requests do not carry over
- [ ] The page does not list dollar caps. The $1,000 / $5,000 figures are unconfirmed
assumptions: Food at meetings is assumed to be for regular member meetings (operational), not events open to the broader CU community.
Hardware is assumed to be stored on campus and used for organizational, not personal, purposes.
The club is assumed to be open to all CU Boulder students (profile says open to all students).
AI tools for students are assumed to possibly count as an organizational use; the page does not confirm this.
missing_items: Number of meetings and food cost per meeting
Specific hardware items, quantities and quotes
Which AI tools, their cost and how they are distributed
Total amount requested (target unknown; SOAC cap not confirmed on page)
